stories.summary: The Trump administration is pressuring European capitals to release their emergency diesel supplies or else face a US diesel export ban, as the White House turns to coercion in efforts to tame surging fuel prices. France, Germany, Britain, Italy, Ireland have all been pressured to draw down supplies , Politico reported. Russia extended its own diesel export ban for at least another month, while China suspended fuel exports for October , a move that will further squeeze global energy supplies. — Brendan Ruberry

articles.summary: Dan Brouillette, Former Secretary of Energy during the first Trump administration and Co-chair of the Torridon Group, says a US diesel export ban would be a “bad idea” because it could eventually force refiners to cut production and raise gasoline prices. Brouillette says reopening the Strait of Hormuz is the most important near-term step to bringing fuel prices down and argues markets need confidence that it will remain open. Brouillette thinks constrained US refining capacity is contributing to diesel scarcity and remains a longer-term infrastructure problem. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
